findings.note: The new test's plural name overstates its coverage, and the reader it does not cover reads the same file with a two-byte-smaller cap. TestReadersAcceptOneMiBLines exercises only runchain.ReadRuns; internal/fsm/record/record.go:156 reads the very same <root>/.metareview/runs.jsonl (record.go:62) with sc.Buffer(make([]byte,0,1<<20), 1<<20) - no +2 - which is precisely the case the duplicated comment at runchain.go:13-16 explains bufio rejects. I demonstrated it empirically in a scratch copy: writing the exact fixture shape this test writes (a row of exactly 1048576 bytes plus LF) and calling record.Exists returns "bufio.Scanner: token too long", so a row that runchain, state, findings and reviewlog all accept makes both record.Exists and record's terminal append fail permanently, with no repair path. This is a known cross-shard item (shard-00 and shard-0a raised it against earlier plans) and is still unfixed at HEAD; recording it here because runchain_test.go is this shard's chunk. Fix: share one constant and one scanner helper across the five readers, or rename the test to the single reader it covers.

findings.note: Gate detail that misdescribes its own failure. internal/fsm/gate/gates.go:136 reports ERR_BUGS_REMAIN with Detail "0 of 0 bugs unfixed" when all_fixed is evaluated on a snapshot where nothing was ever found, because converge.AllFixed is false for an empty AllFound by design. An operator reading that line in the audit sees a self-contradictory sentence: the gate says bugs remain and the count says none do. The real reason is "no bugs were ever found, so 'all fixed' cannot be true". gate_test.go:45 pins the code but only asserts Detail != "", so the wording is unconstrained. Not reachable in the shipped sdlc-loop (verify is only entered through confirmed_nonempty, and the spec notes this at fsm-core.md:35), which is why this is low rather than medium, but it is reachable in any user workflow that gates on all_fixed earlier. Suggest a distinct sentence for the len(AllFound)==0 case.

findings.note: Provenance comment names the wrong one of the reference's two _strip_fences implementations. internal/fsm/judge/prompts.go:455 says stripFences "is the reference's _strip_fences (no pre-trim, model_router path)", but harnesseval@19ff9a8 has two: model_router.py:23 returns s.strip() unconditionally (outside the fence branch), while judge.py:42 strips only inside the branch. The Go body matches judge.py, not model_router; what it takes from the model_router path is only the absence of a caller pre-trim. I checked both against the sibling repo. There is no behavioural consequence - encoding/json skips leading and trailing whitespace, so an unfenced verdict with surrounding whitespace decodes identically either way, and the spec's J2 case (leading whitespace before a fence -> parse error) holds for all three implementations - so this is a documentation accuracy issue only, on a comment whose whole purpose is to name the source being mirrored.
